extracted.intended_audience: Wikipedia readers and editors (general readers, students, and contributors interested in sociology/religion)
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia encyclopedic entry explaining the sociological concept of disenchantment (Entzauberung), its history, critiques, and related concepts. The page is aimed at general readers and contributors who may edit or improve the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encyclopedic style / avoid personal reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: The article currently contains a maintenance notice: 'This article is written like a personal reflection, personal essay, or argumentative essay that states a Wikipedia editor's personal feelings or presents an original argument about a topic.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewrite in an encyclopedic style: remove personal feelings and original arguments, present information neutrally, summarize published sources rather than asserting editors' own views. The page's template explicitly asks: 'Please help improve it by rewriting it in an encyclopedic style.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations / verifiability
rubrics_metrics.description: A section-level notice: 'This section needs additional citations for verification. Please help improve this article by adding citations to reliable sources in this section. Unsourced material may be challenged and removed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add inline citations to reliable sources (news, newspapers, books, scholar, JSTOR, etc.) to support statements. The page includes 'Find sources: "Disenchantment" – news · newspapers · books · scholar · JSTOR (December 2016)' as suggested source types. Unsourced assertions should be sourced or may be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of language and date formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Hidden category notes: 'Use dmy dates from February 2021' and 'Use Oxford spelling from February 2021. All Wikipedia articles written in British English with Oxford spelling.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When editing, conform to the article's locale conventions: use day-month-year (dmy) date format and British English with Oxford spelling throughout the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article maintenance: flagging and addressing style issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The article carries maintenance categories such as 'Wikipedia articles with style issues from September 2022' and 'All articles with style issues.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the flagged style problems (tone, organization, sourcing) to remove maintenance templates. Follow Wikipedia's manual of style and relevant project conventions for organization, lead section, headings, and citations to resolve style issue tags.
